title: Fix 'error: externally-managed-environment' when running pip install
summary: Homebrew Python on macOS refuses pip installs into the system-wide Python. Install the package into its own virtual environment, or with pipx for command-line apps, instead.

aliases.text: pip install error externally managed environment
pip install python package mac venv
pip install ошибка externally managed mac
pip не ставит пакет на маке
установить python пакет в виртуальное окружение mac

prerequisites: Python 3 installed, for example from Homebrew

steps.explain: Check which Python runs in Terminal. A path under /opt/homebrew or /usr/local means Homebrew Python, which blocks pip installs into the system-wide Python.
steps.expect: A path such as /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 (Apple Silicon) or /usr/local/bin/python3 (Intel).

steps.explain: Create a virtual environment: a private folder with its own Python and pip, so the package stays out of the system Python. Skip this step if you use the pipx alternative in step 3.

placeholders.name: VENV_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder for the new environment, in your home folder

steps.expect: The command finishes with no output, and the folder <VENV_DIR> now exists.

steps.explain: Install the package with the environment's own pip. Using the full path to the environment's Python means you do not have to activate it first.

placeholders.name: VENV_DIR
placeholders.description: The environment folder created in the previous step

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Name of the Python package to install

steps.expect: The last line starts with 'Successfully installed' and names the package.

alternatives.explain: For a command-line app (for example httpie), pipx installs it in its own hidden environment and puts the command on your PATH. Needs pipx first (brew install pipx). Does not need the virtual environment from step 2.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Name of the command-line app to install

verify.expect: Lines starting with 'Name:' and 'Version:' for the package.

warnings: Do not add --break-system-packages to pip, even if the error message suggests it. It overrides the protection and can break Python tools installed with Homebrew.
Do not use sudo pip install: it writes into the system Python and bypasses this protection.
